14 and E16 as revise. The strongest candidates are the ones whose controls
and conclusions are already matched to a bounded descriptive question inside the supplied
P01 formulation family. E13 remains the best direct-system
comparison because it combines anchored and normalized donor contrasts
with Ar and no-amine attribution controls while explicitly avoiding overclaim that normalization makes
TEA and TEOA equivalent. E15 and E17 remain strong because
they ask descriptive questions that their measurements can actually answer
: donor-dependent CO2-responsive solution-state signatures and
donor-by-water interaction, respectively. E18 is also shortlist-worthy because
it has been successfully narrowed to a bulk-covariate screen with validated
descriptors rather than mechanistic proof.
By contrast, E14 still suffers from signal-assignment ambiguity and
multi-property isotope perturbation, and E16
still depends on a chemically underdetermined
replacement-base arm whose rescue logic is intrinsically non-exclusive. Across
the set, direct evidence mainly supports staying within the P01
recipe family, while most mechanistic rationale is transferred with
clear limits from other cobalt or bipyridine-related systems. A sensible
research sequence would therefore prioritize the shortlisted
bounded screens first, then use the revise candidates only if those simpler comparisons justify
more assignment-limited specialist follow-up."}
